lines.line: node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints Hello, <name>! in upper case, for example HELLO, ADA!
lines.evidence: Tried a build that ignores --shout. bin/greet.js already drops every arg starting with '--' when it looks for the name, so `--shout Ada` currently prints 'Hello, Ada!'. The proof run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` must print HELLO, ADA!, so a build that never uppercases fails it. A build that uppercases only part of the string (e.g. 'HELLO, Ada!') also fails, because the line says the whole greeting is upper case.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: Tried a build that always shouts, or that treats any '--' flag as shout. The proof `node bin/greet.js Ada` must print 'Hello, Ada!', so an always-shout build fails it. The existing cli test checks the same output.

lines.line: docs/index.md documents the --shout option with an example
lines.evidence: The request says the option must show up on the published docs site so support can point people at it. .github/workflows/pages.yml runs actions/upload-pages-artifact with path: docs and then actions/deploy-pages. There is no Jekyll or any other build step (no actions/jekyll-build-pages, no configure-pages), and docs/ holds only index.md and no index.html. Pages deployed from an Actions artifact serves files exactly as uploaded, so the site root has no rendered page and index.md is at best a raw file at /index.md. Wrong build that meets this line: add a '--shout' section with an example to docs/index.md and change nothing else. The line passes on reading the file, but support still has no rendered docs page to send people to. Two readers will grade 'shows up on the published docs site' differently, and the outcome's claim that docs/ 'is published' is never checked: the issue puts the live page out of scope as a non-goal. Missing line: something checkable before merge that makes docs/ produce a served page, e.g. a docs/index.html or a Jekyll build step in pages.yml.

lines.line: npm test passes and includes a test that runs greet with --shout
lines.evidence: Wrong build that meets the words: add `test('shout', () => { execFileSync('node', ['bin/greet.js', '--shout', 'Ada']); })`, or one that asserts only that the output is non-empty. That test 'runs greet with --shout' and passes, but it would still pass if --shout printed 'Hello, Ada!' unchanged (which the current code already does). So it gives no regression protection. The line needs to say the test asserts the output is 'HELLO, ADA!\n'.

result.wrong_build: Add a --shout check in bin/greet.js that uppercases the greeting, so `--shout Ada` prints HELLO, ADA! and plain `Ada` prints Hello, Ada!. Add a '--shout' paragraph with an example to docs/index.md. Add a test that runs `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` but makes no assertion on its output, so npm test passes. Every expect line is met. Still wrong in two ways: (1) the test would pass even if shouting broke, so there is no real regression test; (2) pages.yml uploads docs/ raw, with no Jekyll/markdown build and no index.html, so the published site has no rendered docs page showing --shout. The request's 'shows up on the published docs site' is not delivered, and no line before merge catches it.
